prompt: Implement an object pool that recycles a fixed number of Buffer objects: acquire reuses a released buffer (wiped clean) before ever constructing a new one, and release accepts only a buffer genuinely checked out of that pool.
explanation: A pool trades allocation for bookkeeping: two lists, one of checked-out objects and one of idle ones, and every object must be in exactly one of them. Membership has to be tested with reference identity (==) rather than equals, because two distinct buffers could otherwise look interchangeable and a stranger or a double release would corrupt the counts. Resetting a buffer on the way out -- not on the way in -- guarantees the caller always receives clean state no matter how the previous user left it.
hints: Keep two lists, one for checked-out buffers and one for free ones, plus an int counting how many Buffer objects you have ever constructed.
acquire has three branches in order: reuse from the free list (calling reset() on it), construct a new one while created < capacity, or return null.
release must find the exact object with == in a loop over the live list. If no element matches -- a stranger, or one already released -- return false without touching either list.
